learningObjectives: Reference configuration with correct delimiters and inheritance/overrides.
Distinguish wildcard flexibility from unique identification.
Create and value reusable-block parameters at the intended scope.
Choose CP, PL or B by linkage, not presumed technical/business audience.

elements.text: Custom TCP reference syntax is {CP[Name]}: CP is outside square brackets. Inherited values can be overridden lower in the hierarchy. Built-in Browser configuration and custom data parameters have different roles; both use the documented configuration scope.

Independent example: configure BaseURL on the common parent and replace hard-coded uses with {CP[BaseURL]}. A child override can intentionally use another environment. This is not restricted to technical audiences or exclusively technical data.

Wildcard * can match varying text in supported values, table names and identification parameters. Independent example: Discount* tolerates a suffix; it can also match multiple labels. Inspect uniqueness and escape a literal asterisk. Adding a column or a wildcard does not create missing application controls.

Business parameters summarize selected reusable-block data. Create a Business Parameter Container on the RTSB, add a parameter and link the relevant TestStepValue with {PL[Name]}. Set the concrete value in the consuming block reference. Names must not contain dots.

CP reads configuration; PL links a business parameter; B recalls a buffer. Business parameters can include URL data, so the prefix choice is about scope and linkage, not whether a value sounds technical.

Independent example: two references can supply different Email values while sharing the same block. Editing a reference value is separate from editing the reusable definition; definition changes can still affect consumers.

examPitfalls.title: Inheritance
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming every child always uses the parent value.

examPitfalls.title: Delimiters
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Putting CP itself in square brackets.

examPitfalls.title: Reference scope
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a reference value edit as a shared-definition edit.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the selected object and field.

examPitfalls.title: Parameter audiences
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating TCP and Business Parameters as user-role restrictions.

examPitfalls.title: Wildcard ambiguity
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming matching a suffix proves uniqueness.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect candidates and escape literal asterisks.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Forty steps in TestCases under one common folder use the same hard-coded URL. With no local overrides, which approach supplies one inherited value without changing reusable-block definitions?

options.text: Define BaseURL on the common folder and replace literal uses with {CP[BaseURL]}.
Assume a Business Parameter on an unrelated block replaces every literal URL automatically.
Use a Dynamic Value expression to auto-generate the URL at runtime.
Hard-coded values cannot be parameterized in Tosca — individual TestStep edits are required.

practiceQuiz.hint: First replace literal uses with the correct lookup.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A common TCP can serve the explicitly converted uses; this does not automatically rewrite hard-coded strings.

optionExplanations.A: A common lookup supplies the intended value once literal uses are converted.
optionExplanations.B: An unrelated block parameter cannot rewrite arbitrary literals.
optionExplanations.C: A generator does not establish this configured environment value.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Fifteen child TestCases need the same BaseURL with no local overrides. How many definitions are needed on their common folder?

options.text: 15 times — once per TestCase.
Once on the folder — it is inherited by all child TestCases.
Twice — once on the folder and once on the first TestCase.
TCPs cannot be defined on folders; they must be defined on individual TestCases.

practiceQuiz.rationale: One parent definition can serve these descendants.

optionExplanations.B: A parent definition serves the stated scope.
optionExplanations.C: The first child does not require a second definition.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Different references to one shared RTSB need different ProductName values without editing the reusable definition. Which mechanism fits that scope?

options.text: A Self-Defined Test Configuration Parameter (TCP).
A Dynamic Value expression.
A Business Parameter linked to the relevant TestStepValue and valued at each block reference.
A Standard Module attribute.

practiceQuiz.hint: The required scope is the consuming block reference.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Business parameters expose data at that reference scope; they are not reserved for a particular user role.

optionExplanations.A: A folder/case lookup does not itself expose the requested reference field.
optionExplanations.B: Generation is not the stated per-reference input.
optionExplanations.C: This provides the requested consumer-specific field.
optionExplanations.D: A technical attribute is not this parameter mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester drags a Business Parameter named 'Email' from a Library RTSB onto a TestStepValue field. What link is created in the value field?

options.text: {CP[Email]}
{BP[Email]}
{B[Email]}
{PL[Email]}

practiceQuiz.rationale: PL is the link prefix for this parameter, distinct from configuration and buffer lookup.

optionExplanations.B: This is not the documented link prefix.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Three TestCases all reference the same 'Precondition' Reusable TestStepBlock from a Library. Each needs to log in with a DIFFERENT email and password. How do Business Parameters solve this?

options.text: Define Business Parameters on the RTSB once; set each TestCase's own values at its RTSB Reference — the Library stays unchanged.
Edit the RTSB in the Library three times, once per TestCase.
Resolve the Reference in all three TestCases and hard-code the credentials.
Create three separate Libraries, one per credential set.

practiceQuiz.hint: Define once on the Library, value per TestCase at the Reference.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Supply each reference’s values without changing the shared definition for this data change.

optionExplanations.B: Repeated shared-definition edits affect the same shared block.
optionExplanations.C: Resolution removes sharing unnecessarily for this task.
optionExplanations.D: Separate libraries are unnecessary solely for different values.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A supported table-column name is 'Discount:'. Which candidate tolerates varying suffixes while still requiring a uniqueness check?

options.text: Rescan the entire Module to force the option to appear.
Use Discount* as the column-name candidate, then inspect other matches.
Create a Business Parameter named Discount.
Use {CP[Discount]} in the value field.

practiceQuiz.hint: Flexible matching can broaden the result.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The wildcard tolerates the suffix; it does not prove a single match or supply a missing control.

optionExplanations.A: A rescan is not needed just for flexible name matching.
optionExplanations.B: This handles the suffix with validation of matches.
optionExplanations.C: Naming a parameter does not identify the column.
optionExplanations.D: CP reads a configured value rather than inherently matches this name.

quickRecap.value: Define linkage on the block and values in references.
Value contents and job role do not determine the prefix.
